message.content:
Based on my thorough analysis, I've found the root cause of the issue. The `MySensorsHVAC` class in `homeassistant/components/climate/mysensors.py` has a hardcoded `SUPPORT_FLAGS` that always includes all three temperature feature flags (`SUPPORT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE`, `SUPPORT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE_HIGH`, `SUPPORT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE_LOW`). This causes the frontend to always display three separate temperature controls regardless of whether the node actually supports both heating and cooling setpoints.

When a MySensors HVAC node has only one setpoint (e.g., only `V_HVAC_SETPOINT_HEAT` for a heating-only thermostat), the frontend still shows all three temperature controls because the `supported_features` property unconditionally returns all flags. The `target_temperature_high` and `target_temperature_low` properties may return `None` when the corresponding setpoint values don't exist, but the frontend still shows empty/multiple temperature controls.

The fix is to make `supported_features` dynamically check which setpoint values are available in `_values` and return the appropriate feature flags.
